haiku-low.q1: MySQL first, in one transaction with an outbox row. Postgres is applied inline after commit. If Postgres fails, the request still succeeds and the outbox row remains for repair.
haiku-low.q2: Only when the incoming row's version is higher than the stored version (WHERE users.version < EXCLUDED.version), and the id is not in users_tombstones.
haiku-low.q3: Every running instance must report users_write_mode as mysql_dual with none missing, then 5 more minutes must pass. Instances can disagree for up to 30 seconds after a change.
haiku-low.q4: One worker holds a Postgres advisory lock, copies 2000-row batches, pauses while replica lag exceeds 5 s or is missing or stale, and waits at least 0.5 s between batches.
haiku-low.q5: Reads: the step 5 compare gate (one clean pass, zero persistent mismatches) and then the ramp holds. Source switch: 3 days at 100% Postgres reads, a clean compare within 24 h, outbox oldest row under 1 minute, healthy Postgres, and a recorded go decision.
haiku-low.q6: A row in the MySQL users_pg_outbox table, written in the same transaction as the user write. The users-sync-worker re-reads the row from the MySQL primary and applies it with pg_copy, within about 12 seconds.
haiku-low.q7: Deletes insert a tombstone. pg_copy takes LOCK TABLE users_tombstones IN SHARE MODE and skips tombstoned ids, so a copy and a delete cannot interleave and resurrect the row.
haiku-low.q8: In Postgres migration_progress (name, last_id, rows_copied, updated_at), updated in the same Postgres transaction as each batch's upserts. It stops when the read returns zero rows and the outbox is empty, or the flag is reverted.
haiku-low.q9: The compare job walks 5,000-id windows, comparing id, email, name, plan and version, plus Postgres-only and tombstoned-but-present ids. Persistent differences become outbox rows; equal-version content mismatches page a human.
haiku-low.q10: Database fence rows: writers read them FOR SHARE, and the coordinator's UPDATE waits for them. If the drain is not empty at 45 s, revert to mysql_dual and active. Pause lasts the longer of 30 s and the drain time.
haiku-low.q11: Postgres users_id_seq assigns new ids. During the pause it is set to GREATEST(current, MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT + 1,000,000). For rollback, MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT is raised above the highest Postgres id if needed.
haiku-low.q12: Postgres writes flow to MySQL via pg_outbox, with reverse drain and reverse compare. Rollback takes 90 s or less: pause, drain, fix AUTO_INCREMENT if needed, switch states. It ends when step 10 starts, at least 14 days after source_since.

sonnet.q1: MySQL first: one MySQL transaction (fence read FOR SHARE, the write, an outbox row), then after commit the row is applied to Postgres inline via pg_copy (250 ms timeout, circuit breaker). If Postgres fails or the breaker is open, nothing happens and the request still succeeds; the outbox row stays.
sonnet.q2: Only if the incoming row's version is higher than the existing Postgres row's version (users.version < EXCLUDED.version), and the id is not in users_tombstones. Deletes ignore the version rule.
sonnet.q3: users_write_mode=mysql_dual must be reported by app_flag_value on every running instance, with none missing from the series, and then 5 more minutes must pass; the backfill starts automatically once this gate has held 5 minutes. Instances can disagree for up to 30 s after a flag change (30 s refresh).
sonnet.q4: Before each batch it reads mysql_replica_lag_seconds; if lag is above 5 or the metric is missing/stale it sleeps 10 s and rechecks. It reads from the replica, in batches of 2000 rows, with a 0.5 s minimum between batches (about 5 to 6 hours total), and skips ids with a pending outbox row. Only one worker holds a Postgres advisory lock.
sonnet.q5: Reads to Postgres (step 6): backfill done (zero rows read and outbox empty) and one full compare pass with 0 persistent mismatches; each ramp stage needs its hold time with healthy PG error rate, p99 latency, fallback rate and 0 compare mismatches. Source switch (step 7): reads 100% on Postgres for at least 3 days (clock starts when app_flag_value shows 100 on every instance), a compare pass with 0 mismatches within the last 24 h, oldest outbox row under 1 minute, Postgres cluster healthy, and the go decision recorded.
sonnet.q6: A row in the MySQL outbox table users_pg_outbox, written in the same MySQL transaction as the user write (so it is durable even if the app dies after commit). The users-sync-worker (2 replicas) polls it every 2 s, claims rows older than 10 s, re-reads the current row from the MySQL primary and applies it with pg_copy (or deletes plus tombstone if gone), retrying with backoff. Repair takes about 12 s, and an alert fires if the oldest row is over 5 minutes old.
sonnet.q7: Deletes write a tombstone (id only) into Postgres users_tombstones, and pg_copy skips ids in users_tombstones. pg_copy first takes LOCK TABLE users_tombstones IN SHARE MODE, which conflicts with a delete's tombstone insert, so a copy and a delete cannot interleave. Tombstones are kept permanently, and the tombstone is written even if the row was never in Postgres.
sonnet.q8: In Postgres table migration_progress(name, last_id, rows_copied, updated_at), updated in the same Postgres transaction as each batch's pg_copy upserts, so last_id is exactly the last completed batch. The backfill stops when the read returns zero rows and the outbox is empty (also stops if the gate flag is reverted).
sonnet.q9: The compare job (step 5, also nightly during the read ramp). It walks 5,000-id windows comparing (id, email, name, plan, version), and also finds Postgres-only ids and ids tombstoned yet still in MySQL. A window with differences is re-read from the MySQL primary and Postgres after 60 s; only persistent differences count, and each becomes an outbox row, repaired automatically. An equal-version mismatch with different content cannot be repaired: it is a bug, pages a human and blocks the gate.
sonnet.q10: A database fence: each write reads a migration_state fence row FOR SHARE in its own transaction (MySQL row for mysql/mysql_dual, Postgres row for pg_dual/pg_only); if not active it raises WritesPaused (503 with Retry-After). The coordinator's UPDATE takes an exclusive lock and waits for in-flight writers. With MySQL paused and Postgres standby, any instance regardless of flag gets 503. If it runs long: abort is allowed only before sub-step 4; if the drain is not empty at t=45 s, set MySQL back to active and the flag to mysql_dual, total pause 75 s or less. After sub-step 4, go forward or use step 9 rollback.
sonnet.q11: Postgres, via the sequence users_id_seq (created in step 1). During the switch pause the coordinator runs setval(GREATEST(current, mysql_auto_increment_counter + 1,000,000)), which is at or above every id MySQL issued including deleted ones, so no collision with tombstones. On rollback, if the MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT counter is not above the highest Postgres id, run ALTER TABLE users AUTO_INCREMENT=... before reactivating MySQL.
sonnet.q12: Postgres is the source and every write goes through pg_outbox, which the reverse drain (users-sync-worker) applies to MySQL with the same version rule, plus a mirrored copy function after commit; MySQL failures never fail the request. Watch outbox age and compare passes. Rollback (90 s or less): set users_write_mode=mysql_dual and Postgres state active→paused; drain pg_outbox to empty; fix MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT if needed; set MySQL standby→active and Postgres paused→standby. Abort only before sub-step 4. The option lasts at least 14 days after source_since; it ends with step 10 (pg_only, allowed after 14 days), where writes stop going to MySQL and the reverse drain is stopped; the final end is dropping MySQL users in step 11.
